title: pricing-packaging-scratchpad-riley-2026-03
content:
Quick back-of-envelope notes for pricing/packaging. Personal scratchpad - rough numbers, assumptions, open questions.

Context: trying to reconcile unit economics for hosted API (per-token) + Dedicated/reserved offers. Goal: simple PLG-friendly tiers that map to cost drivers (tokens, qps, KV cache hit rate) and surface upgrade paths to Dedicated/Private.

ASSUMPTIONS (subject to validation)
- Baseline serving cost (amortized infra + infra ops + storage + SRE): $0.60 / GPU-hour-equivalent for an efficient quantized LLM serving path (this is a placeholder; need infra to sanity-check)
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (avg across request distribution): 30 tokens/sec sustained (varies widely; use 30 as conservative)
- Hours per month: 720
- Effective tokens per GPU-month = 30 tokens/sec * 3600 sec/hr * 720 hr = 77,760,000 tokens (~77.8M)
- Infra cost per token = $0.60 / 77.8M ≈ $7.7e-09 (~$0.0000000077) per token (compute only)
- Add other overheads (control plane, storage, network, SRE, billing, margin) -> multiply by 6x to get all-in ~ $4.6e-08 (~$0.000000046) per token
- Round to design-friendly numbers: cost per 1k tokens = $0.000046 -> ~0.00005 per 1k tokens (compute+ops).

Practical pricing check (market comps)
- Competitor public rates range widely; many charge $0.002–$0.05 per 1k tokens depending on model/quality. Our all-in cost above is very low vs market, leaving room for margin and discounts for committed usage.

SIMPLE UNIT ECONOMICS SUMMARY
- All-in cost per 1k tokens (baseline) ≈ $0.00005 (note: still likely underestimates - double-check GPU-hour and tokens/sec).
- If we price hosted generation at $0.005 / 1k tokens (intro), gross margin >> 90%.
- Elastic customers (uncommitted) should pay a premium vs committed customers.

EXAMPLE CUSTOMER SCENARIOS (1 month)
1) Hobby app: 500k tokens/month -> cost to us ≈ 500 * $0.00005 = $0.025 -> price at $0.005/1k = $2.50/month.
2) Startup: 50M tokens/month -> cost to us ≈ 50,000 * $0.00005 = $2.50 -> price at $0.005/1k = $250/month.
3) Scale app: 2B tokens/month -> cost = 2,000,000 * $0.00005 = $100 -> price at $0.004/1k (volume discount) = $8,000/month.

Note: these cost numbers are intentionally tiny because per-token compute cost with batching/prefix cache is very low when amortized across large batch sizes. The biggest additional costs are engineering support, storage for logs, egress, SLO guarantees, and quota management.

TIER IDEAS (hosted API)
- Free / Starter: 10k tokens / month free, then pay-as-you-go at $0.01/1k for first month (promotional), then baseline. Aimed at fast product experiments and onboarding.
- Hobby: included 1M tokens/mo, $5/mo. Overage $0.005/1k. No SLA, limited qps, community support.
- Startup: included 50M tokens/mo, $249/mo. Overage $0.004/1k. Higher qps, analytics 30d, team seats (3).
- Scale: included 2B tokens/mo, $7,500/mo. Overage $0.002/1k or negotiated. SLA 99.9, higher retention, priority support.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: custom pricing; reserved capacity and committed spend with volume discounts (e.g., 30–60% off list depending on commit and term). Includes private deployment options, custom compliance, and longer retention.

Notes on numbers:
- Starter/Hobby pricing intentionally higher per-1k to reduce free tier abuse and encourage conversion.
- Volume-based breakpoint discounts at 100M, 500M, 2B tokens.
- Consider a separate price track for embeddings (higher compute per token typically) - treat embeddings at Xx generation price or flat per-embedding vector.

Dedicated/reserved packaging (back of envelope):
- Example: customer needs 10 GPUs reserved (for guaranteed throughput). If committed monthly cost per GPU-hour = $0.50 (our cost) and we charge $1.50/GPU-hour -> 10 GPUs * 24 * 30 * $1.50 = $10,800/month. Offer stepped discounts for >3/6/12 month terms.
- Alternatively express as included tokens: 10 GPUs -> ~777.6M tokens/month (using 77.8M/GPU-month) -> price X per token derived from r/hours. But many buyers prefer capacity-centric (GPUs) not token counts.

Pricing levers to expose in product/console
- Per-route model selection (model A priced higher than model B)
- Priority tiers (latency/throughput SLAs) priced as a premium
- Caching multiplier: if customer uses prefix caching aggressively, show effective token discount on bill (e.g., bill only for unique generated tokens after cache hits)
- Batch/throughput discounts: encourage batch-friendly endpoints via cheaper per-token rates during high-util windows

Open questions / TODO items
- Validate tokens/sec/GPU numbers with infra/benchmarks across our model catalog (quantized and fp16 variants). Current numbers are placeholders.
- Real per-GPU hourly cost (including amortized capital and ops).
- Embeddings: measure tokens per embedding call vs runtime and create a per-vector price (or keep as per-1k tokens but call it out).
- How to handle function-calling/structured outputs where token accounting is ambiguous (prompt vs model vs tool output)?
- Billing granularity: round to nearest 1k tokens or 100 tokens? Simpler UX = 1k tokens.
- Free tier abuse mitigation (rate limits, credit card verification, quota caps).

Quick sensitivity checks
- If tokens/sec is 60 (better batching), tokens/GPU-month = 155.5M -> infra per-token halves -> more margin or lower list price.
- If GPU-hour cost is $2 (higher infra) -> cost per token increases ~3x -> still probably well below market list.

Next steps
1) Sync with infra (Ali, Priya) to get real GPU-hour and realistic tokens/sec by model profile (sparse/long-context).
2) Run a small internal dashboard computing current customer token mix to map expected margins across existing usage patterns.
3) Draft an internal proposal with two pricing skews: "PLG friendly" (low entry price, higher overage) vs "enterprise-first" (higher included tokens, lower per-token overage).
4) Validate embedding pricing separately with applied-ml.

Random notes / UX ideas
- Show "effective cost" slider in console so users can see how batching/caching affects their expected monthly bill.
- Provide a committed discount calculator and example contracts for sales (3/6/12 month).
- Consider fixed-price connectors for high-volume streaming use-cases (chat interfaces) so customers can anchor budget to throughput not tokens.

End of scratchpad. Keep iterative - will update after infra sync (aiming to get numbers by 2026-03-10).
